summary: Full backend + frontend E2E test of the Qumështorja VITA landing page. Backend: created pytest suite (14 tests) covering /api/ health, POST/GET /api/contact (persistence + 422 validation matrix) and POST/GET /api/newsletter (duplicate 409, invalid email) — 13 passed, 1 skipped (documents non-normalized email). Frontend: verified loader dismissal, navbar + all 7 nav anchors, glass-on-scroll, 17-product catalog with 6 category tabs, 7 filter chips, live search + no-products state, product modal (nutrition/ingredients/sizes/storage/related swap), featured slider (next/prev/dots/auto-rotate/view-details/find-stores), quality counters (20+/280+/3,000+/6), 5 recipe tabs, 4 timeline entries, testimonial auto-carousel, gallery lightbox, scroll-to-top, mobile menu + mobile modal, contact form -> POST /api/contact 200 + success toast + form reset, newsletter -> 200 then 409 'already subscribed' toast. Both submissions verified persisted via GET APIs. 40/40 images loaded, zero console/page errors, no HTTP >= 400, no mobile horizontal overflow.

minor.issue: Email is not normalized/lowercased before the duplicate lookup, so 'a@b.com' and 'A@B.com' both subscribe (two rows for one address). No unique index on newsletter.email either, so concurrent posts can also duplicate.
No min_length on name/message — an empty-string name and message are accepted (200) at API level; only the UI guards this.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: the lightbox close button is unclickable — Playwright normal click times out with 'navbar intercepts pointer events', and elementFromPoint over the close button returns data-testid=navbar. Root cause: <main className="relative z-10"> in App.js creates a stacking context, so overlays inside it (gallery lightbox z-[1000], product modal z-[1000]) cannot rise above the fixed navbar (z-[950] progress bar / z-[900] navbar) which sit outside main. Lightbox can only be closed by clicking the backdrop.

Same stacking-context defect makes the navbar (and scroll-to-top button) paint on top of the open product modal on both desktop and mobile — visible in screenshots. The modal close button happens to sit below the navbar strip so it still works, but the overlay looks broken.

issues: Sonner toasts render top-center on top of the navbar and hide the 'Recipes/About/Quality' links while visible; move to top-right/bottom-right or offset below the navbar.

Live search matches only name + short text, so searching 'milk' returns 3 of the 6 milk-ish SKUs and misses 'Vita Qumësht 3.2%' / 'Vita Kos'; include category and tags (and Albanian synonyms) in the match.
Filter chips are not toggleable — clicking an already-active chip keeps it active; the user must click the 'All' chip to clear.

action_items: Fix overlay stacking: remove z-10 from <main> in App.js or render ProductModal/Gallery lightbox into a React portal at document.body with z-index above the navbar (or hide/lower the navbar while an overlay is open). This currently blocks closing the gallery lightbox via its X button.
Reposition/offset sonner toasts so they don't cover the navbar links.
Normalize newsletter emails to lowercase and add a unique index on newsletter.email.
Broaden product search to include category/tags so 'milk' also matches 'Vita Qumësht'.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js: `<main className="relative z-10">` traps every child overlay in a z-index:10 stacking context — this is the single root cause of the navbar painting over modals/lightbox.
FeaturedSlider.jsx: the 4.2s autoplay interval never pauses on user interaction (prev/next/dot click), so a slide can flip out from under the user mid-read; reset the timer inside go().
server.py: POST /api/contact returns the mutated insert dict; safe today only because response_model=Contact strips the injected _id. Prefer inserting a copy to avoid future leakage.
Contact.jsx/Footer.jsx duplicate the axios+toast submit pattern; consider a shared hook. Inputs also lack `required`/aria-invalid — validation is toast-only.

rca_of_the_issue: Gallery lightbox close button unclickable: App.js wraps all sections in `<main className="relative z-10">`, which establishes a stacking context. The lightbox's z-[1000] is therefore resolved *within* main (effective z-index 10 at root level), while Navbar (z-[900]) and the scroll progress bar (z-[950]) are siblings of main at root level and paint above it. The close button is positioned at right-6/top-6, i.e. underneath the fixed navbar, so the navbar receives the pointer events. Repro: open the site, scroll to Gallery, click gallery-item-0, click lightbox-close -> click times out ('navbar intercepts pointer events'); document.elementFromPoint over the button returns the navbar. Mitigation: portal overlays to document.body or drop z-10 from <main>.
